GLOBE: Geometry-Led Online Behavioral Early Exit via Unit-Sphere Trajectories

Xinyue Peng    Zhenlin Liang    Meng Cai    Hua Wang Affiliation: Moore Threads Email: meilong@mthreads.com
Abstract

Chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning can improve problem solving, but models often keep generating after the correct answer is already reachable; the extra steps raise serving costs and may replace a correct intermediate result with an incorrect one. We propose GLOBE (Geometry-Led Online Behavioral Early Exit), an online, training-free algorithm that terminates the model’s CoT process early. GLOBE embeds each completed reasoning segment as a point on a unit sphere and reads the shape of the resulting semantic trajectory. GLOBE first applies a trial phase that generates short trial answers in a separate branch, stopping the main stream on an accepted trial after checking confidence against a threshold. If generation continues, a trajectory phase stops the stream once this path repeatedly reverses direction with little net progress. On five benchmarks including mathematical reasoning, tool calling, and agent memory, GLOBE cuts output tokens by 49.7% and active end-to-end wall time (E2E) by 51.0% across two models, and achieves a five-task average of 80.58%, comparable to Full CoT.

1 Introduction

Allocating additional test-time computation to chain-of-thought reasoning can substantially improve complex decision making and problem solving in language models (Wei et al., 2022; Wang et al., 2023; Snell et al., 2025). However, longer traces have uncertain marginal value while imposing costs in token throughput, request concurrency, and end-to-end latency. Long-form reasoning models often keep generating after the correct answer is already reachable, and the extra steps can replace a correct intermediate result with an incorrect one, a behavior known as overthinking (Chen et al., 2025; Wu et al., 2026; Han et al., 2026; Sui et al., 2025). Early exit is therefore an online allocation decision: from the current prefix, an inference system must decide whether to stop or purchase more computation without observing the future continuation.

Early-exit methods monitor different signals. Reflection-marker methods trigger trial answers and stop when local confidence passes an acceptance test (Yang et al., 2026); output-distribution methods compare continuing with emitting a thinking-close token at syntactic boundaries (Song et al., 2026; Wei et al., 2026); answer-convergence methods wait for sampled answers to stabilize (Liu and Wang, 2025); and other work inspects step-level redundancy, confidence dynamics, sufficiency, or internal activations (Min et al., 2026; Hosseini et al., 2026; Sun et al., 2026; Xiang et al., 2026; Liu et al., 2026). A separate line of work shortens reasoning by training with length-aware objectives or by fixing a decoding budget (Arora and Zanette, 2025; Aggarwal and Welleck, 2025; Muennighoff et al., 2025). These signals are not interchangeable: a trial tests whether the current prefix is ready to answer, whereas a long trace can keep changing even after local confidence is already high.

We ground the comparison in measurements by replaying the full chain-of-thought traces of BFCL v4 Live (Patil et al., 2025) offline and reproducing two types of trigger points: trial answers launched at candidate signals, such as a reflection marker like Wait; and cuts of the reasoning stream, which is split into segments with a stop triggered at every cut. For each trigger point we record the same three quantities: whether the answer reaches high confidence (mean token probability q>0.9q>0.9), whether that answer is correct, and the average confidence over those points. Figure 1 shows that the two families are offset in time: trials at candidate signals peak early in the trace and then decay, whereas cuts of the reasoning stream keep improving until late in the trace. Confidence decides whether a trial answer is accepted, not when the trial signal stops being useful. The open question is therefore whether a controller can tell, during generation, whether the reasoning is still making progress or is looping back on itself.

To this end, we propose GLOBE, a training-free online algorithm over a single reasoning stream. It launches short trial answers at candidate signals and embeds each completed segment, so that generation traces a path on a unit sphere. Early in the trace, a confident trial answer ends generation; later, the trajectory decides, and the stream stops once it keeps retracing what it has already covered.

We make three contributions:

  • •

    We observe that trial-answer stopping and reasoning-stream-cut stopping are effective in different regions of the trace: trial answers work best early and decay with depth, whereas stream cuts improve later. GLOBE therefore introduces a phase switch rather than concatenating them: trial confidence asks whether the current prefix is answer-ready, while spherical trajectory geometry asks whether reasoning is still advancing.

  • •

    We introduce a spherical trajectory representation that transforms abstract semantic progress into measurable geometric properties. Each completed segment is embedded and normalized to a point on the unit sphere, where net displacement signals progress and repeated directional reversals with little net displacement indicate repetition. The trajectory criterion relies only on the angles between segment embeddings. It therefore requires neither complex semantic evaluation nor language-specific vocabulary or syntax.

  • •

    GLOBE cuts output tokens and E2E time by about half while keeping its frequent early exits reliable. Across two models and five benchmarks for tasks such as mathematical reasoning, tool calling, and agent memory, GLOBE averages 80.58% on the five-task score, comparable to 80.04% for Full CoT, while cutting output tokens by 49.7% and active E2E time by 51.0%. On Qwen’s GSM8K analysis runs, early exits correct 29.8% of Full CoT errors while making 0.94% of Full CoT-correct answers incorrect.

2 Related Work

Efficient reasoning and test-time compute.

Chain-of-thought and test-time scaling improve difficult reasoning by allocating more inference computation (Wei et al., 2022; Snell et al., 2025), but longer traces may repeat established conclusions or overturn a correct intermediate answer (Chen et al., 2025; Wu et al., 2026). One line of work intervenes at training time, using supervised or reinforcement learning with length-aware objectives so that the model itself emits shorter traces (Arora and Zanette, 2025; Aggarwal and Welleck, 2025; Han et al., 2026). Another leaves the weights untouched and controls length at inference time, through a fixed budget, budget forcing, concise prompts, or a non-thinking mode (Muennighoff et al., 2025; Ma et al., 2025); Sui et al. (2025) survey this space. These approaches control how much reasoning is generated, whereas we study a training-free online algorithm that decides, from the current instance’s evolving history, whether to purchase more computation.

Online early stopping from local evidence.

Inference-time methods commonly inspect intermediate answers or decoding signals. Answer Convergence stops when predictions from partial traces stabilize (Liu and Wang, 2025). Certaindex estimates the stability and certainty of intermediate answers to adapt compute (Fu et al., 2025), and trained hidden-state probes predict answer correctness to support early exiting (Zhang et al., 2025a). DEER uses reflection markers to propose trial answers and exits when their token confidence is high (Yang et al., 2026); ThinkBrake instead monitors the margin between the best continuation token and the thinking-close token (Song et al., 2026), while RCPD tracks the rank of that token at sentence boundaries and force-closes the thinking segment once one of a few rules distilled from offline reasoning-dynamics analysis is satisfied (Wei et al., 2026). DTSR prompts the model to assess thought sufficiency at reflection points (Xiang et al., 2026), while CoDE-Stop and REFRAIN use confidence or redundancy dynamics over multiple checkpoints (Hosseini et al., 2026; Sun et al., 2026). GLOBE uses such pointwise local evidence only in its trial phase.

Trajectory-level and deployable controllers.

Representation-level methods move beyond a single answer score. PUMA detects semantic redundancy between reasoning steps and verifies candidate exits with an answer probe (Min et al., 2026); NEAT monitors neuron activation dynamics without answer rollouts (Liu et al., 2026). Both compare representations locally, at a step or a pair of steps, rather than describing the shape of the accumulated trace. Latent-Trajectory signals summarize traces from the model’s hidden states, but select among sampled traces rather than stop a single one (Vilas et al., 2026). Deployment adds a second requirement: in tool-using and agentic settings a stop must preserve the parser-visible action and cross-turn state (Yao et al., 2023; Schick et al., 2023; Patil et al., 2025), and the cost of a controller includes the trial requests and repeated prefix computation it adds, not only the tokens it retains. GLOBE addresses both: it stops a single stream online from the geometry of its accumulated text-embedding trajectory, and it reports active E2E time alongside retained tokens under each task’s native protocol.

3 Methodology

3.1 GLOBE Overview

Figure 2 gives an overview of GLOBE, which embeds each completed reasoning segment as a point on a unit sphere and reads the shape of the resulting semantic trajectory. The trial phase generates short trial answers in a separate branch at candidate signals such as Wait and checks their confidence against a threshold. A highly confident trial answer is accepted and stops the main stream; otherwise, it is discarded and the main stream keeps generating. A reversal is a step of the trajectory that moves partly back along the previous step. Once reversals have accumulated, the stream enters the trajectory phase and stops launching trials. In this phase, the trajectory stop ends the stream once the trajectory repeatedly reverses direction with little net progress, that is, a small net displacement relative to its path length. The reasoning is then circling over content it has already covered. After an accepted trial or a trajectory stop, GLOBE generates the final answer from the retained prefix. If neither occurs, the model ends its reasoning naturally and then answers.

3.2 Candidate-Signal-Triggered Trial Answers

The trial phase aims to decide whether the current reasoning prefix r≤tr_{\leq t} already suffices to answer. This prefix consists of the reasoning tokens generated up to step tt. The decision is made before reasoning ends. For this purpose, GLOBE launches short trial answers at sparse candidate signals. It uses their confidence as the criterion.

The controller supports two types of candidate signals. The first type consists of the two most representative textual markers in the reasoning text. These markers are Wait and Actually. Wait marks a pause to check the current reasoning. Actually marks a re-verification of it. The second type is the task-native thinking-close marker </think>. The controller does not wait for this marker to be generated. Instead, it detects the marker as soon as it enters the top-5 next-token candidates. Thus, the reasoning stream is not closed early. The fact that the model is ready to answer becomes available as a signal, and the reasoning can still continue.

Trial answers are generated in a separate branch, leaving the main reasoning stream uninterrupted. When a signal triggers, the controller freezes the exact prefix, appends a prompt gg that elicits a direct answer, and issues one trial request. The request returns a trial answer y~\tilde{y} of length m≤τtrialm\leq\tau_{\mathrm{trial}}; the model’s predictions are sharply concentrated when the prefix suffices and more dispersed otherwise (Yang et al., 2026). Let xx be the task input, 𝒱\mathcal{V} the vocabulary, and ℋθ\mathcal{H}_{\theta} the LM head with parameters θ\theta. The logits at position ii (1≤i≤m1\leq i\leq m, with the preceding trial tokens y~<i\tilde{y}_{<i}) and their largest entry are

𝒐i=ℋθ​(x,r≤t,g,y~<i),oi⋆=maxv∈𝒱⁡oi,v,\bm{o}_{i}=\mathcal{H}_{\theta}\bigl(x,r_{\leq t},g,\tilde{y}_{<i}\bigr),\qquad o_{i}^{\star}=\max_{v\in\mathcal{V}}o_{i,v},

where oi⋆o_{i}^{\star} corresponds to the token chosen by greedy decoding. The confidence of a trial is the mean over positions of the softmax probability of that token:

q=1m​∑i=1mexp⁡(oi⋆)∑v∈𝒱exp⁡(oi,v).q=\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\frac{\exp\bigl(o_{i}^{\star}\bigr)}{\sum_{v\in\mathcal{V}}\exp\bigl(o_{i,v}\bigr)}. (1)

A trial is accepted when qq exceeds the confidence threshold τconf\tau_{\mathrm{conf}}. In this case, the prefix is deemed sufficient to answer. The decision rests on the model’s own predictive distribution, not on the correctness of the answer.

After a trial is accepted, the system runs the continuation procedure. First, it cancels the main reasoning stream and discards everything after the frozen point. Second, it re-issues the retained prefix to the same serving endpoint. Thus, its prefix cache is reused. Third, it appends </think> and generates the final answer under the original prompt and native parsing rules. A rejected trial is discarded and leaves the main reasoning stream unaffected. Trial requests are accounted for separately. Appendices A.1 and A.3 give the exact prefix boundaries, edge cases, and cost accounting.

3.3 Unit-Sphere Trajectory Representation

Fewer trial answers are both confident and correct late in reasoning (Figure 1), so the next signal must come from the reasoning content itself: is the chain advancing, or is it returning to what it has covered? Prior work shows that embeddings encode semantics: the squared norm of a word embedding carries its information gain, a result extending to contextualized embeddings (Oyama et al., 2023), while semantic relations are reflected in the directions of their difference vectors (Mikolov et al., 2013; Ethayarajh et al., 2019). Since our decision concerns the relation between successive reasoning segments rather than the information gain carried by any one of them, and our encoder’s cosine-similarity objective makes that relation angular (Zhang et al., 2025b), we normalize each segment embedding onto the unit sphere, so that advance and return are read from the angles alone.

The geometric observer runs alongside the main reasoning stream. The segmenter splits the reasoning text rr into segments s1,s2,…s_{1},s_{2},\ldots at sentence-ending punctuation and newlines. It merges adjacent fragments until each completed segment has at least the minimum length LminL_{\min} (in characters). This prevents over-fragmentation. Each completed segment is then encoded into a semantic vector by the embedding model. Appendix A.2 describes the segmenter. Embedding overlaps with generation; its request time is at most 13.6%13.6\% of per-item wall time in the profiled Qwen runs (Appendix D.2). Appendix D.9 gives encoder details and results with smaller encoders.

Let JJ be the number of completed segments and zj∈ℝdz_{j}\in\mathbb{R}^{d} the semantic vector of segment sjs_{j}, where dd is the embedding dimension. We normalize this vector as uj=zj/‖zj‖2u_{j}=z_{j}/\|z_{j}\|_{2}, where ∥⋅∥2\|\cdot\|_{2} denotes the Euclidean norm. The reasoning trajectory is the point sequence (uj)j=1J(u_{j})_{j=1}^{J} on the unit sphere 𝕊d−1={u∈ℝd:‖u‖2=1}\mathbb{S}^{d-1}=\{u\in\mathbb{R}^{d}:\|u\|_{2}=1\}. Its chordal displacements are ξj=uj+1−uj\xi_{j}=u_{j+1}-u_{j}. The controller incrementally maintains the needed entries of the Gram matrix S=[Sa,b]S=[S_{a,b}], with entries Sa,b=⟨ua,ub⟩S_{a,b}=\langle u_{a},u_{b}\rangle for a,b∈{1,…,J}a,b\in\{1,\dots,J\}, where ⟨⋅,⋅⟩\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle denotes the Euclidean inner product. The chord length ‖ua−ub‖2=2−2​Sa,b\|u_{a}-u_{b}\|_{2}=\sqrt{2-2S_{a,b}} depends only on the angle. Thus, the statistics below are functions of the Gram matrix SS alone. They are invariant under orthogonal transformations of the embedding space and under positive rescaling of the raw embeddings zjz_{j}. Each new segment therefore requires only O⁡(d)O(d) time to update these quantities.

To detect changes of direction, we compute the inner products of consecutive chordal displacements:

κj=⟨ξj,ξj+1⟩=12​(‖uj+2−uj‖22−‖ξj‖22−‖ξj+1‖22)=Sj,j+1+Sj+1,j+2−Sj,j+2−1.\kappa_{j}=\langle\xi_{j},\xi_{j+1}\rangle=\tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(\|u_{j+2}-u_{j}\|_{2}^{2}-\|\xi_{j}\|_{2}^{2}-\|\xi_{j+1}\|_{2}^{2}\bigr)=S_{j,j+1}+S_{j+1,j+2}-S_{j,j+2}-1. (2)

Here κj\kappa_{j} is defined for 1≤j≤J−21\leq j\leq J-2, and κj<0\kappa_{j}<0 means one directional reversal. By the polarization identity, this is equivalent to the reasoning not continuing along its previous direction (Appendix B.2). We count reversals by KJ=∑j=1J−2𝟏[κj<0]K_{J}=\sum_{j=1}^{J-2}\mathbf{1}[\kappa_{j}<0]. Here, 𝟏​[⋅]\mathbf{1}[\cdot] is the indicator function.

Once the reversals have accumulated, we also need to decide whether the reasoning is going in circles instead of making progress. For this purpose, we first look at how far the trace has traveled and how far it has actually advanced. These distances are the path length and the start-to-end displacement:

ℓJ=∑j=1J−1‖ξj‖2=∑j=1J−12−2​Sj,j+1,δJ=‖uJ−u1‖2=2−2​S1,J.\ell_{J}=\sum_{j=1}^{J-1}\|\xi_{j}\|_{2}=\sum_{j=1}^{J-1}\sqrt{2-2S_{j,j+1}},\qquad\delta_{J}=\|u_{J}-u_{1}\|_{2}=\sqrt{2-2S_{1,J}}. (3)

We define the net-displacement ratio as QJ=δJ/ℓJQ_{J}=\delta_{J}/\ell_{J} when ℓJ>0\ell_{J}>0, and set QJ=1Q_{J}=1 when ℓJ=0\ell_{J}=0. A smaller value means that the trace returns more relative to the path it has traveled.

3.4 Phase Switch and Trajectory Stop

Let J⁡(t)J(t) be the number of segments completed by step tt, and write Kt=KJ⁡(t)K_{t}=K_{J(t)} and Qt=QJ⁡(t)Q_{t}=Q_{J(t)} for the reversal count and the net-displacement ratio at that point. The constants KphaseK_{\mathrm{phase}}, KoscK_{\mathrm{osc}}, and τQ\tau_{Q} are the phase-switch, oscillation, and net-displacement-ratio thresholds. The early-exit indicator at step tt is

et={𝟏[q>τconf],Kt<Kphase​and a signal triggers at ​t,𝟏[Kt≥KoscandQt≤τQ],Kt≥Kphase,0,otherwise.e_{t}=\begin{cases}\mathbf{1}[q>\tau_{\mathrm{conf}}],&K_{t}<K_{\mathrm{phase}}\ \text{and a signal triggers at }t,\\ \mathbf{1}[K_{t}\geq K_{\mathrm{osc}}\ \text{and}\ Q_{t}\leq\tau_{Q}],&K_{t}\geq K_{\mathrm{phase}},\\ 0,&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases} (4)

GLOBE exits at the first step with et=1e_{t}=1. The first case is the trial phase. Here, the signal is a candidate signal of Section 3.2. Once KtK_{t} reaches the phase threshold KphaseK_{\mathrm{phase}}, the stream enters the trajectory phase of the second case. In this phase, no further trials are launched. Also, no exit is possible until KtK_{t} reaches the oscillation threshold KoscK_{\mathrm{osc}}. A trajectory stop is placed at the boundary of the latest completed segment. If et=0e_{t}=0 throughout, reasoning ends at the model’s own termination. Both early exits execute the continuation procedure of Section 3.2. Appendix A.5 lists the operating thresholds.

4 Experiments

4.1 Experimental setup

Benchmarks and models.

We evaluate five benchmarks: commonsense question answering on CSQA (Talmor et al., 2019), role-play character fidelity on Character-LLM (Shao et al., 2023), grade-school mathematics on GSM8K (Cobbe et al., 2021), tool calling on BFCL v4 Live (Patil et al., 2025), and long-horizon agent memory on BFCL v4 Agent Memory (Patil et al., 2025), whose KV, Vector, and Recursive Sum backends are scored separately. We use two instruction-tuned thinking models from different families and parameter scales, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (Qwen Team, 2026), a mixture-of-experts model with 35B total parameters, and Gemma-4-12B-it (Gemma Team and others, 2026), which we call Qwen and Gemma. Accuracy or exact match is the native metric of the four accuracy-style benchmarks; for Character-LLM, a fixed judge applies a four-aspect adaptation of the original rubric and we report the resulting normalized acting score (NAS), defined in Appendix C.1. We also report average retained output tokens and active task-level end-to-end wall time (E2E).

Baselines.

Nothink disables the thinking channel and answers directly, bounding the cost of reasoning from below (Ma et al., 2025). Full CoT leaves thinking unconstrained and serves as the quality reference. DEER (Yang et al., 2026) watches reflection markers, issues a trial answer at each marker, and exits the stream once that trial answer is confident. ThinkBrake (Song et al., 2026) uses no trial answers: at sentence boundaries it compares the log probabilities of continuing and of emitting </think>, and stops on a margin criterion. RCPD (Wei et al., 2026) also uses no trial answers and tracks the rank of </think> at sentence boundaries, closing the thinking segment once one of a few rules distilled from an offline reasoning-dynamics analysis is satisfied. Each baseline follows its method-native contract.

4.2 Main results

Overall performance.

Table 1 compares GLOBE with the Nothink and Full CoT controls and with the early-exit baselines of Section 4.1. GLOBE attains the highest five-task average on both models, reaching 83.08% on Qwen and 78.08% on Gemma against 82.42% and 77.66% for Full CoT. The reduction holds on every task: averaged over the ten model–task pairs, output tokens fall by 49.7% and E2E time by 51.0%, and the five-task average output-token count falls from 3141 to 931 on Qwen and from 1386 to 813 on Gemma.

Comparison with early-exit baselines.

DEER loses 5.7 accuracy points on GSM8K and 5.1 on CSQA in Gemma; its stop needs a reflection marker where the trial answer is already decidable, which is not guaranteed across models. ThinkBrake is the most conservative: no task’s accuracy deviates from Full CoT by more than 3.6 points, and it stays below Full CoT in both five-task averages. RCPD is the cheapest controller on Qwen in tokens and E2E, averaging 791 tokens and 2660 s, but it sacrifices accuracy: a 78.44% five-task average, 4.64 points below GLOBE and 15.7 points below Full CoT on BFCL v4 Live, suggesting its rank rule can trigger before the answer settles. No baseline reaches the Full CoT five-task average on either model, while GLOBE exceeds it on both.

GLOBE is stable across models and datasets.

The Nothink–Full CoT gap shows that thinking matters most on Agent Memory, with gaps of 20.5% and 10.1% on the two models, while the gap is 0.4% and 0.3% on GSM8K and at most 3.6% on the other three tasks. GLOBE’s worst task is 2.1 points below Full CoT, and it spends fewer tokens and less E2E time than Full CoT in all ten model–task cells. The baselines diverge: on the five-task average, DEER falls 1.341.34 points below Full CoT on Qwen and 2.482.48 below it on Gemma, whereas ThinkBrake falls 1.301.30 and 0.600.60 points below, respectively. RCPD is the weakest baseline on Qwen yet the strongest on Gemma. RCPD’s savings are equally model-dependent, removing 71.9% of output tokens on Qwen but only 3.2% on Gemma.

4.3 Ablation study

Table 2 removes one component of GLOBE at a time and compares each variant with the GLOBE row of Table 1. Removing any component lowers the three-task average accuracy on both models, by up to 11.311.3 points. The three tasks span the difficulty tiers of Section 4.2: GSM8K depends on thinking least, Agent Memory most, and BFCL v4 Live in between; Appendix Tables 8 and 9 extend the sweep to CSQA and Character-LLM.

The trajectory stop controls token cost.

Removing it is the most costly ablation: all six token cells rise, by a factor of 2.622.62 on Qwen and 2.302.30 on Gemma. Without it, the Agent Memory output on Qwen grows from 2040 to 9181 tokens. The largest observed accuracy gap is 32.932.9 points on GSM8K in Gemma, followed by 11.111.1 on Agent Memory in Qwen; Gemma Agent Memory gains 4.74.7 points, so the trajectory stop contributes more than any other component. Appendix D.5 shows that the Gemma GSM8K loss comes from traces that never close within the token budget. The criterion matters wherever the trace stalls: the stream closes once the trajectory reverses repeatedly with little net displacement. Geometry judges whether the trajectory still advances without certifying correctness, so dropping the stop lets generation continue into a post-retrieval restatement that resembles oscillation.

Removing the phase switch costs accuracy.

The phase switch is one-way: once the cumulative reversal count reaches KphaseK_{\mathrm{phase}}, the controller permanently retires trial answers and only the trajectory stop can close the stream; removing it lets trial answers return in the trajectory phase. It costs an average of 2.92.9 accuracy points on Qwen and 4.54.5 on Gemma. On Qwen the loss concentrates on Agent Memory, which drops by 7.97.9 points, while GSM8K and BFCL v4 Live save at most 14%14\% of tokens for at most 0.40.4 accuracy points; on Gemma every task loses accuracy, by 3.23.2 to 5.45.4 points. Removing it changes average token use by at most 10%10\% yet consistently lowers the three-task average, so the savings cannot offset the accuracy loss.

Trial answers and the τQ\tau_{Q} gate are jointly required.

Trial answers freeze the prefix at a candidate signal such as Wait and generate a short answer in a separate branch, accepted only when its confidence exceeds a threshold; the τQ\tau_{Q} gate vetoes trajectory-stop candidates when Qt>τQQ_{t}>\tau_{Q}. Removing either component lowers accuracy in all twelve model–task combinations, by up to 5.15.1 points, and the three-task averages by up to 4.44.4. The cheapest Qwen variant drops the τQ\tau_{Q} gate and uses 0.93×0.93\times the tokens of GLOBE, but loses accuracy on all three tasks; on Gemma, dropping either component saves up to 11%11\% of tokens on BFCL v4 Live and Agent Memory for up to 5.15.1 accuracy points. No cell is simultaneously cheaper and more accurate than GLOBE: the trials test whether the current prefix already supports an answer, and the gate vetoes stops that would come too early.

4.4 Stop reliability

Early stopping can recover some Full CoT errors.

Figure 3a joins Full CoT with GLOBE by item: harm is the share of Full CoT-correct items that GLOBE stops early and answers incorrectly, and rescue is the share of Full CoT-wrong items that GLOBE stops early and answers correctly. GSM8K is the least thinking-dependent task, so answers are usually already determined: harm is rare at 0.94%0.94\% and rescue reaches 29.8%29.8\%. On BFCL v4 Live, a tool call must keep its choice, call structure and arguments consistent, so a settled-looking prefix can still become a different call; harm is 4.17%4.17\% and rescue 9.56%9.56\%. On Agent Memory the two rates are at 10.8%10.8\% and 24.9%24.9\%, because the stateful task also carries the run-to-run divergence of the memory contents into the join.

GLOBE converts the most early stops into correct answers.

Figure 3b splits each Qwen task into correct early stops in green, incorrect early stops in orange and items left to close naturally in grey, so the green band is the share of items stopped early and answered correctly. GLOBE has the largest green band on all three tasks, at 95.2%95.2\% on GSM8K, 53.3%53.3\% on BFCL v4 Live and 27.7%27.7\% on Agent Memory. DEER requires a reflection marker plus a confident trial, capping its green band at 62.3%62.3\% on GSM8K and 39.0%39.0\% on BFCL v4 Live. ThinkBrake triggers only when closing the segment comes within a fixed margin of continuing; on GSM8K the closing decision stays far behind continuing at every sentence boundary, so it is marked never stops. On BFCL v4 Live it reaches only 3.9%3.9\%. RCPD stops more than DEER or ThinkBrake but converts less: on GSM8K and BFCL v4 Live its green bands are 89.5%89.5\% and 46.5%46.5\%, against 95.2%95.2\% and 53.3%53.3\% for GLOBE, and only 59.8%59.8\% of its BFCL stops are correct. Under GLOBE, 16.8%16.8\% of BFCL v4 Live items are stopped early with a wrong answer, against 31.2%31.2\% under RCPD. On Agent Memory it stops only 30.5%30.5\% of items for a 19.6%19.6\% green band against 27.7%27.7\%. RCPD thus shows both failure modes of a surface trigger: low conversion on BFCL v4 Live and rare stops on Agent Memory.

4.5 Operating-point evidence

Thresholds are selected using the Qwen BFCL v4 Live 2,2512{,}251 items reported in Table 1. Excluding this model–task pair, the remaining nine pairs still reduce output tokens by 48.4%48.4\% and E2E time by 52.5%52.5\%.

The reversal-count thresholds are Kphase=4K_{\mathrm{phase}}=4 and Kosc=8K_{\mathrm{osc}}=8.

Figure 4a shows the two evidence lanes that delimit the phase switch. Trial conversion peaks at index 4 with 42.5%42.5\% of trials accepted and correct, then falls to 17.4%17.4\% at index 6, while the cut yield rises steadily with the reversal count and reaches 34.7%34.7\% at K=8K=8 across 1,0641{,}064 trajectories. Although K=11K=11 yields a nominally higher 37.7%37.7\%, it relies on only 236236 trajectories. We fix Kphase=4K_{\mathrm{phase}}=4 as the phase-switch threshold, so that trials retire once the reversal count reaches four, and select Kosc=8K_{\mathrm{osc}}=8 from the cut lane, where the trajectory evidence is strongest with adequate support.

The net-displacement-ratio threshold is set to τQ=0.14\tau_{Q}=0.14.

Figure 4b plots accuracy and retained reasoning tokens against τQ\tau_{Q}. We loosen the gate to enable more early stops while preserving accuracy. Raising the gate from 0.060.06 to 0.140.14 lifts trajectory stops from 699699 to 1,0671{,}067, a 52.6%52.6\% increase, and cuts retained reasoning tokens from 322.0322.0 to 240.9240.9, a 25.2%25.2\% reduction. At 0.140.14, we observe the highest accuracy of 79.96%79.96\% with 1,8001{,}800 correct items. Its token count is also within 1.5%1.5\% of the lowest value in the sweep, so 0.140.14 is close to the best on both accuracy and cost. Beyond 0.140.14, tokens stay near their minimum while accuracy falls below the peak, yielding little additional saving. We therefore select 0.140.14 to balance quality and token savings.

5 Conclusion

Early-exit methods usually decide from local statistics, yet whether reasoning is still making progress is a property of the whole trace. We propose GLOBE, an online, training-free algorithm that embeds each completed reasoning segment as a point on a unit sphere and reads the shape of the resulting semantic trajectory. Its trial phase stops the main stream on an accepted trial, and its trajectory phase stops it once the trajectory repeatedly reverses direction with little net progress. Across two models and five benchmarks, GLOBE cuts output tokens by 49.7% and E2E time by 51.0% while achieving a five-task average of 80.58% against 80.04% for Full CoT. The ablations show that every component matters: removing any one lowers the three-task average on both models, by up to 11.3 points. On GSM8K with Qwen, GLOBE stops 98.9% of traces early and answers 96.3% of them correctly. Combining confident trial answers with trajectory geometry keeps aggregate quality comparable to Full CoT at about half the output tokens and E2E time.

AI use statement

In this work, we use generative AI tools to aid and polish writing, including drafting and editing prose, translation, and maintaining the LaTeX source and bibliography. Generative AI tools also assist with implementing and debugging experiment code and providing feedback on experimental design. We have reviewed all AI-assisted work, and we take responsibility for the final content of this work, including text, claims, and artifacts produced with the aid of generative AI.

Appendix A Implementation details

This appendix specifies the controller exactly as it runs: the execution contract and accounting (A.1), the segmenter and geometry updates (A.2), degenerate cases (A.3), the per-increment control order with Algorithm 1 (A.4), the reference configuration (A.5), the per-model and per-task details of the trial branch (A.6), and the analysis-only spherical diagnostics (A.7).

A.1 Execution Contract and Notation

GLOBE uses the following notation and contracts for its online policy. The input xx comprises the user instruction, dialogue history, and tool schemas. The task-native template produces c⁡(x)=Tok⁡(Render⁡(x))c(x)=\operatorname{Tok}(\operatorname{Render}(x)), and the autoregressive model defines pθp_{\theta} over 𝒱\mathcal{V}. The reasoning prefix is r=(r1,…,rT)r=(r_{1},\ldots,r_{T}); scloses_{\mathrm{close}} is the task-native thinking-close marker, such as </think>; and yy is the visible continuation containing the final answer or structured tool call. At each streaming step t≤Tt\leq T, policy π\pi observes r≤tr_{\leq t} and decides what to do.

The system maintains one continuous main reasoning stream and may launch bounded independent auxiliary trial-answer requests. Retained output tokens, discarded trial tokens, repeated prefix computation, request count, and total active E2E time are accounted for separately. Token-count claims count only retained tokens rather than collapsing distinct overheads into one quantity. Rejected trial text is discarded from its independent branch and never written to the main reasoning stream. An exit taken by the controller cancels the main stream, re-issues the retained prefix to the same serving endpoint so that its cached key-value state is reused, appends the task-native thinking-close marker, and generates the final answer or tool call through task-native formatting and parsing. A natural close preserves the original main stream.

At most BB trial answers may be launched per sample. Trial answers are disabled permanently when either KJK_{J} reaches KphaseK_{\mathrm{phase}} or the launched-trial count reaches BB. Since the phase-switch check precedes candidate-signal evaluation on each increment, the increment causing the switch cannot launch another trial answer. Setting B=0B=0 disables trials for a task without a matching scaffold while retaining trajectory-level geometry.

A.2 Segmentation and Geometry Updates

The reference segmenter parses RtR_{t} online, placing boundaries at sentences and newlines (sent80). Adjacent fragments are merged until each completed segment has at least Lmin=80L_{\min}=80 characters. The unfinished tail is not embedded. Newly completed segments are batched and truncated to at most 1200 characters before embedding; requests occur only when a segment completes.

The main stream maintains a latch for the thinking-close marker. When </think> is absent from the top-5, only the rising-edge latch resets; the growing prefix is not re-encoded. Re-encoding occurs only when an absent-to-present rising edge (Appendix A.3) satisfies the remaining candidate-signal conditions, avoiding quadratic recomputation while the marker is absent. The exact prefix of a Wait or Actually candidate signal ends immediately before the marker and excludes the marker itself; the exact prefix of a thinking-close rising edge contains all reasoning text generated through the current observation, because the delimiter has not been emitted.

A.3 Formula Boundaries and Degenerate Cases

Reversal statistics require at least three completed segments. With too few completed segments, the controller conservatively sets KJ=0K_{J}=0 and QJ=1Q_{J}=1, preventing a trajectory stop. The ratio is QJ=δJ/ℓJQ_{J}=\delta_{J}/\ell_{J} for ℓJ>0\ell_{J}>0 and QJ=1Q_{J}=1 for ℓJ=0\ell_{J}=0.

If mt=0m_{t}=0, no token can be scored. The trial answer is rejected because confidence is undefined. Non-finite values, dimension-incompatible vectors, or other embedding failures are handled fail-closed by permanently disabling the geometric observer for that sample. Any exception or error during a trial answer also rejects that trial.

The thinking-close marker has an absent-to-present rising edge when

sclose∉Top5t−1andsclose∈Top5t.s_{\mathrm{close}}\notin\operatorname{Top5}_{t-1}\quad\text{and}\quad s_{\mathrm{close}}\in\operatorname{Top5}_{t}. (5)

The task-specific scaffold elicits a direct answer. Acceptance runs no separate format or schema check: the confidence score covers every token the trial returns, complete or not, and downstream task-native parsers provide the final format safety.

A.4 Online Control Order and Policy Formalization

For each streaming increment, the controller first commits completed segments and updates geometry, then applies the phase switch, evaluates the trajectory-stop condition, and finally evaluates at most one trial answer if still in the trial phase. Thus, the increment first reaching KphaseK_{\mathrm{phase}} cannot launch another trial; a trajectory stop consumes no trial attempt; and rejected trial tokens never enter the retained prefix.

With J⁡(t)J(t) denoting the latest completed segment, the policy is

π⁡(t)={trajectory stop,ϕt=trajectory phase∧KJ⁡(t)≥Kosc∧QJ⁡(t)≤τQ,trial-answer stop,ϕt=trial phase∧candidate signal holds∧qt>τconf,natural close,main stream emits ​sclose,continue generation,otherwise.\pi(t)=\begin{cases}\text{trajectory stop},&\phi_{t}=\text{trajectory phase}\ \wedge\ K_{J(t)}\geq K_{\mathrm{osc}}\ \wedge\ Q_{J(t)}\leq\tau_{Q},\\ \text{trial-answer stop},&\phi_{t}=\text{trial phase}\ \wedge\ \text{candidate signal holds}\ \wedge\ q_{t}>\tau_{\mathrm{conf}},\\ \text{natural close},&\text{main stream emits }s_{\mathrm{close}},\\ \text{continue generation},&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases} (6)

Here ϕt∈{trial phase,trajectory phase}\phi_{t}\in\{\text{trial phase},\text{trajectory phase}\}. Candidate-signal conditions include a 32-token cooldown, the limit BB, discourse transitions, and a deduplicated thinking-close-marker rising edge.

A natural close may occur in either phase. Actual emission of scloses_{\mathrm{close}} retains the original stream without truncation or re-encoding, closes pending trial branches and side diagnostics, and generates yy with native task parameters. A top-5 rising edge only proposes a trial; it is not natural termination.

A.5 Reference Configuration and Variant Boundaries

The reference thresholds Kphase=4K_{\mathrm{phase}}=4, Kosc=8K_{\mathrm{osc}}=8, and τQ=0.14\tau_{Q}=0.14 are the reference operating point. Table 3 lists the task-specific settings, budgets, and concurrency, including Character-LLM which uses no trials. The main stream uses temperature=0, enable_thinking=true, stream=true, and top_logprobs=5. BFCL v4 Live and Agent Memory run at concurrency 4 with a 16,384-token retained budget, and GSM8K and CSQA run at concurrency 8 with an 8,192-token budget; all methods use the same concurrency within each task. Every request allows two retries with a 0.5-second base interval and a 300-second timeout. These are serving controls, not stopping rules.

Each sample permits at most B=10B=10 trials of at most τtrial=20\tau_{\mathrm{trial}}=20 tokens. The scaffold appended to the frozen prefix is \n**Final Answer**\n\boxed; trial generation ends at the first closing brace or after 20 tokens, and the confidence of Eq. (1) averages the chosen-token probability over every returned token, including the first one and a length-truncated tail, with τconf=0.9\tau_{\mathrm{conf}}=0.9.

The only textual markers are Wait and Actually, matched with and without a leading space. The minimum segment length is Lmin=80L_{\min}=80, embedding input is capped at 1,200 characters, each completed segment permits one close-marker trial, and trials have a 32-token cooldown. Coincident textual and close-marker candidate signals are merged.

Trajectory representation uses Qwen3-Embedding-8B served on a separate vLLM instance. Without geometry, a sample cannot trajectory-stop. Empty trials, missing or misaligned log-probabilities, non-finite values, and zero-norm, non-finite, or dimension-incompatible embeddings are fail-closed: the trial is rejected or geometry is permanently disabled.

A.6 Model- and Task-Specific Details of the Trial Branch

Thinking-close marker.

The close marker is the tokenizer’s own end-of-thinking token: </think> (ID 248069) for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and <channel|> (ID 101) for Gemma-4-12B-it, whose reasoning is returned on a separate reasoning channel. The top-5 rising edge of Eq. (5) is evaluated on this token, and the continuation appends the same token before decoding the visible answer.

One scaffold for every task.

GSM8K, CSQA, BFCL v4 Live, and Agent Memory share the boxed scaffold of Appendix A.5. The trial only has to reveal whether the prefix already commits to an answer, so acceptance never parses the trial text: a trial that starts a number, an option letter, or a function name inside the box is scored the same way. The accepted continuation, not the trial, produces the answer that the task parser reads, so the scaffold never changes the visible output format; for tool calls the continuation is parsed by the serving stack’s native tool-call parser.

Role-play harness.

Character-LLM answers are free-form in-character utterances, so the role-play harness has no trial phase: it embeds completed segments, applies the trajectory stop after a minimum number of completed segments, and answers from the retained reasoning, with a 2,048-token generation budget and a 512-token answer budget. Its thresholds are listed in Table 3.

Prefix reuse.

Trials and continuations are sent to the endpoint that serves the main stream, with prefix caching enabled, so the frozen prefix is not recomputed from scratch. The repeated prefill that a trial or continuation would otherwise cost is recorded per item.

A.7 Intrinsic Spherical Diagnostics (Analysis Only)

Intrinsic Riemannian spherical diagnostics are used only in offline shadow analysis. For x,y∈𝕊d−1x,y\in\mathbb{S}^{d-1},

θ⁡(x,y)=arccos⁡(clip⁡(x⊤​y,−1,1)).\theta(x,y)=\arccos\!\left(\operatorname{clip}(x^{\top}y,-1,1)\right). (7)

For non-degenerate, non-antipodal vectors,

logx⁡(y)=θ⁡(x,y)sin⁡θ⁡(x,y)​(y−cos⁡θ⁡(x,y)​x),\log_{x}(y)=\frac{\theta(x,y)}{\sin\theta(x,y)}\left(y-\cos\theta(x,y)x\right), (8)
PTx→y⁡(w)=w−⟨w,y⟩1+⟨x,y⟩​(x+y),⟨w,x⟩=0.\operatorname{PT}_{x\to y}(w)=w-\frac{\langle w,y\rangle}{1+\langle x,y\rangle}(x+y),\qquad\langle w,x\rangle=0. (9)

Transporting loguj⁡uj+1\log_{u_{j}}u_{j+1} to the tangent space at uj+1u_{j+1} and comparing it with loguj+1⁡uj+2\log_{u_{j+1}}u_{j+2} yields intrinsic turning angle, tangential-velocity change, and acceleration norm; degenerate and antipodal cases are recorded separately. These diagnostics do not affect control. The deployed policy uses only the Gram/chordal-displacement statistics and net-displacement ratio from Section 3.3.

Appendix B Mathematical characterization of the stopping statistics

This appendix provides the detailed mathematical characterizations and formal derivations for the properties of the two stopping signals used by our method. Every statement presented in this section concerns the statistics exactly as they are deployed in the system (as described in Appendix A.5). None of these formulations change the underlying controller logic, and none of them constitutes a statement about the correctness or truthfulness of a model’s generated answer.

B.1 The trial-answer score

Let 𝒱\mathcal{V} be the discrete vocabulary of the language model, and let Δ⁡(𝒱)\Delta(\mathcal{V}) denote the probability simplex over this vocabulary. The total variation distance between two probability distributions P,Q∈Δ⁡(𝒱)P,Q\in\Delta(\mathcal{V}) is defined as TV⁡(P,Q)=12​‖P−Q‖1=supA⊆𝒱|P⁡(A)−Q⁡(A)|\mathrm{TV}(P,Q)=\tfrac{1}{2}\|P-Q\|_{1}=\sup_{A\subseteq\mathcal{V}}|P(A)-Q(A)|. For the next-token distribution at position ii along the trial we write Pt,iP_{t,i}, and we abbreviate the probability of the emitted token as pt,i=Pt,i​(y~i)p_{t,i}=P_{t,i}(\tilde{y}_{i}). Because the trial is decoded at temperature 00, the emitted token is chosen greedily, y~i∈arg⁡maxv∈𝒱​Pt,i​(v)\tilde{y}_{i}\in\arg\max_{v\in\mathcal{V}}P_{t,i}(v), so that pt,i=maxv∈𝒱⁡Pt,i​(v)=‖Pt,i‖∞p_{t,i}=\max_{v\in\mathcal{V}}P_{t,i}(v)=\|P_{t,i}\|_{\infty} is the largest probability of the distribution. If there are ties for the maximum probability, they are broken arbitrarily and do not affect any of the identities below. The deployed scorer then averages this confidence over every returned trial token. Note that an empty trial with mt=0m_{t}=0 is automatically rejected.

We now give the full derivation of the distance to point masses, which yields an equivalent total-variation characterization of the trial score in Eq. (1). Fix any distribution P∈Δ⁡(𝒱)P\in\Delta(\mathcal{V}) and let pmax=‖P‖∞p_{\max}=\|P\|_{\infty}. For any deterministic point-mass distribution δu\delta_{u} concentrated at a single token uu, the ℓ1\ell_{1} distance is evaluated by separating the element uu from the rest of the vocabulary:

‖P−δu‖1\displaystyle\|P-\delta_{u}\|_{1} =|P⁡(u)−1|+∑v≠u|P⁡(v)−0|\displaystyle=|P(u)-1|+\sum_{v\neq u}|P(v)-0|
=(1−P⁡(u))+∑v≠uP⁡(v)\displaystyle=(1-P(u))+\sum_{v\neq u}P(v)
=(1−P⁡(u))+(1−P⁡(u))=2​(1−P⁡(u)).\displaystyle=(1-P(u))+(1-P(u))=2(1-P(u)).

Dividing by 22, the total variation distance to this point mass is exactly TV⁡(P,δu)=1−P⁡(u)\mathrm{TV}(P,\delta_{u})=1-P(u). To find the closest point mass, we minimize over all tokens u∈𝒱u\in\mathcal{V}. The minimum distance is achieved exactly at the modes of PP, yielding minu⁡TV⁡(P,δu)=1−pmax\min_{u}\mathrm{TV}(P,\delta_{u})=1-p_{\max}. This minimum distance coincides with the Bayes 00–11 risk. If we make a randomised prediction Y^∼π\hat{Y}\sim\pi for a true label Y∼PY\sim P, the probability of error is 1−∑vπ⁡(v)​P​(v)1-\sum_{v}\pi(v)P(v). This error probability is bounded below by 1−pmax​∑vπ⁡(v)=1−pmax1-p_{\max}\sum_{v}\pi(v)=1-p_{\max}, with equality holding if and only if the prediction strategy π\pi is fully supported on the modes of PP. Thus, the Bayes 00–11 risk is exactly 1−pmax1-p_{\max}, and it is attained by any decision rule supported on the modes of PP, including the greedy rule. This risk concerns predicting the model’s own next token, not the correctness of the final answer. Furthermore, using the standard definition of the Rényi infinity entropy H∞​(P)=−log⁡‖P‖∞H_{\infty}(P)=-\log\|P\|_{\infty}, we have pmax=exp⁡(−H∞​(P))p_{\max}=\exp(-H_{\infty}(P)), meaning the minimum distance can also be written as 1−exp⁡(−H∞​(P))1-\exp(-H_{\infty}(P)). Applying these identities at each trial position by setting P=Pt,iP=P_{t,i}, the distance to the nearest deterministic distribution is 1−pt,i1-p_{t,i}. Averaging this quantity over the mtm_{t} trial positions yields exactly the complement of Eq. (1).

The total variation distance can equivalently be written using its dual formulation. For any two distributions PP and QQ, TV⁡(P,Q)=12​sup‖f‖∞≤1|𝔼P​f−𝔼Q​f|\mathrm{TV}(P,Q)=\tfrac{1}{2}\sup_{\|f\|_{\infty}\leq 1}|\mathbb{E}_{P}f-\mathbb{E}_{Q}f|, where the supremum is taken over all test functions bounded in magnitude by 11. Consequently, the complement of the confidence score at a given position, 1−pt,i1-p_{t,i}, is a dual-norm distance: it guarantees that no bounded test function evaluated on the next token can separate the predictive distribution Pt,iP_{t,i} from the deterministic law δy~i\delta_{\tilde{y}_{i}} by more than 2​(1−pt,i)2(1-p_{t,i}).

The single-step confidence can also be bounded via collision probabilities. For every distribution PP, the properties of the ℓp\ell_{p} norms dictate that ‖P‖∞2≤‖P‖22≤‖P‖∞\|P\|_{\infty}^{2}\leq\|P\|_{2}^{2}\leq\|P\|_{\infty}, which can be equivalently restated in terms of Rényi entropies as H∞​(P)≤H2​(P)≤2​H∞​(P)H_{\infty}(P)\leq H_{2}(P)\leq 2H_{\infty}(P). To see why this holds algebraically, observe that P⁡(v)≤pmaxP(v)\leq p_{\max} for all vv, so multiplying by P⁡(v)P(v) and summing gives ∑vP​(v)2≤pmax​∑vP⁡(v)=pmax\sum_{v}P(v)^{2}\leq p_{\max}\sum_{v}P(v)=p_{\max}. Conversely, since probabilities sum to 11, the sum of squares is bounded below by the square of the maximum, ∑vP​(v)2≥pmax2\sum_{v}P(v)^{2}\geq p_{\max}^{2}. The quantity ‖P‖22\|P\|_{2}^{2} is exactly the probability that two independent draws from the distribution PP coincide. Therefore, at every trial position ii, the probability that two independent samples agree lies in the interval [pt,i2,pt,i][p_{t,i}^{2},p_{t,i}]. Note that this is a single-pass, per-position quantity; it is not the multi-sample answer agreement measured by self-consistency decoding (Wang et al., 2023).

Moving from single positions to the entire trial sequence, suppose m=mt≥1m=m_{t}\geq 1 and let the sequence Y=(Y1,…,Ym)Y=(Y_{1},\ldots,Y_{m}) be drawn position by position, with each coordinate Yi∼Pt,iY_{i}\sim P_{t,i} sampled from the next-token laws observed along the greedy trial. This product law is a surrogate that keeps the observed laws fixed; it is not the distribution of autoregressive sampling. Because the coordinates are drawn independently from these fixed laws, the probability that the entire sampled sequence matches the greedy trial exactly is the product of the individual probabilities: Pr⁡(Y=y~)=∏i=1mpt,i\Pr(Y=\tilde{y})=\prod_{i=1}^{m}p_{t,i}. From this, we can establish bounds on the sequence-level error probability Pr⁡(Y≠y~)=1−∏i=1mpt,i\Pr(Y\neq\tilde{y})=1-\prod_{i=1}^{m}p_{t,i} in terms of the average confidence qtq_{t}. On the left side, the arithmetic-mean geometric-mean (AM–GM) inequality implies that ∏i=1mpt,i≤(1m​∑i=1mpt,i)m=qtm\prod_{i=1}^{m}p_{t,i}\leq(\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^{m}p_{t,i})^{m}=q_{t}^{m}, which gives 1−qtm≤Pr⁡(Y≠y~)1-q_{t}^{\,m}\leq\Pr(Y\neq\tilde{y}). On the right side, a standard union bound over the positions at which YY might depart from y~\tilde{y} takes the form of the Weierstrass product inequality. Setting ai=1−pt,i∈[0,1]a_{i}=1-p_{t,i}\in[0,1], we have 1−∏i=1m(1−ai)≤∑i=1mai1-\prod_{i=1}^{m}(1-a_{i})\leq\sum_{i=1}^{m}a_{i}, which implies Pr⁡(Y≠y~)≤∑i=1m(1−pt,i)=m⁡(1−qt)\Pr(Y\neq\tilde{y})\leq\sum_{i=1}^{m}(1-p_{t,i})=m\,(1-q_{t}). This establishes the two-sided inequality

1−qtm≤Pr⁡(Y≠y~)≤m⁡(1−qt).1-q_{t}^{\,m}\;\leq\;\Pr(Y\neq\tilde{y})\;\leq\;m\,(1-q_{t}). (10)

The upper bound is practically informative only when it is strictly less than 11, meaning mt​(1−qt)<1m_{t}(1-q_{t})<1. This occurs for short trials, such as generating boxed numerals. However, for a fully accepted 2020-token trial, the upper bound is informative only if qt>0.95q_{t}>0.95. Because of this looseness for longer sequences, the acceptance rule relies on interpreting the average confidence through the per-position identity of Eq. (1), rather than through the sequence-level bound of Eq. (10).

Finally, we address the algebraic choice of the aggregation function over the trial positions. The average confidence in Eq. (1) is the arithmetic member M1M_{1} of the generalized power means Mα=(1m​∑i=1mpt,iα)1/αM_{\alpha}=(\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^{m}p_{t,i}^{\alpha})^{1/\alpha}. The geometric mean M0=exp⁡(1m​∑i=1mlog⁡pt,i)M_{0}=\exp(\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^{m}\log p_{t,i}), used by DEER (Yang et al., 2026), and the minimum M−∞=mini⁡pt,iM_{-\infty}=\min_{i}p_{t,i} are also valid choices. By the monotonicity of power means, they satisfy the ordering M−∞≤M0≤M1M_{-\infty}\leq M_{0}\leq M_{1}. The arithmetic mean M1M_{1} has a distinct robustness property: changing a single position’s probability pt,ip_{t,i} moves M1M_{1} by at most 1/mt1/m_{t}. This constitutes a bounded influence in the sense of Hampel (1974). In contrast, one vanishing probability in the sequence sends the geometric mean M0M_{0} entirely to 00. Bounded influence cuts both ways. On the one hand, a single low-probability formatting token cannot unfairly veto a trial that is otherwise highly peaked. On the other hand, if the threshold is τconf\tau_{\mathrm{conf}}, a single low-probability token cannot forcefully reject the trial either, provided the trial is long enough that mt>1/(1−τconf)m_{t}>1/(1-\tau_{\mathrm{conf}}).

B.2 The unit-sphere trajectory statistics

We now turn to the geometric properties of the trajectory on the unit sphere. Let the embedding space ℰ=(ℝd,⟨⋅,⋅⟩)\mathcal{E}=(\mathbb{R}^{d},\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle) be a real Hilbert space. The normalized segment embeddings form a sequence u1,…,uJ∈𝕊d−1u_{1},\ldots,u_{J}\in\mathbb{S}^{d-1}. Normalization removes the length of the raw embedding vectors and makes every statistic below invariant to their scale, in line with the motivation of Section 3.3. After normalisation, the geometric relationship between any two states uau_{a} and ubu_{b} is entirely encapsulated by their inner product Sa,b=⟨ua,ub⟩S_{a,b}=\langle u_{a},u_{b}\rangle. The distance between them along the straight chord is Da,b=‖ua−ub‖D_{a,b}=\|u_{a}-u_{b}\|. By expanding the squared norm, we see that Da,b2=‖ua‖2+‖ub‖2−2​⟨ua,ub⟩=2−2​Sa,bD_{a,b}^{2}=\|u_{a}\|^{2}+\|u_{b}\|^{2}-2\langle u_{a},u_{b}\rangle=2-2S_{a,b}, so the chord length Da,b=2−2​Sa,bD_{a,b}=\sqrt{2-2S_{a,b}} depends only on the angle θa,b\theta_{a,b} between the vectors, and can be written as 2​sin⁡(θa,b/2)2\sin(\theta_{a,b}/2). We denote the successive chordal displacements by ξj=uj+1−uj\xi_{j}=u_{j+1}-u_{j}. Whenever angles between chords are evaluated, we assume that ξj≠0\xi_{j}\neq 0, meaning that consecutive reasoning segments produce strictly distinct semantic embeddings.

The structural characteristics of the trajectory are fully determined by the inner products. In fact, if two families of points {ua}\{u_{a}\} and {ua′}\{u^{\prime}_{a}\} have the exact same Gram matrix SS, they describe the identical shape. To prove this full Gram determinacy, define a linear map T:∑aca​ua↦∑aca​ua′T:\sum_{a}c_{a}u_{a}\mapsto\sum_{a}c_{a}u^{\prime}_{a}. For any linear combination, its squared norm is ‖∑aca​ua‖2=∑a,bca​cb​Sa,b\|\sum_{a}c_{a}u_{a}\|^{2}=\sum_{a,b}c_{a}c_{b}S_{a,b}, which equals ‖∑aca​ua′‖2\|\sum_{a}c_{a}u^{\prime}_{a}\|^{2} since the Gram matrices match. Thus, TT is well defined and isometric on span⁡{ua}\operatorname{span}\{u_{a}\}. By standard linear algebra, this map extends to a global linear isometry of the full space ℰ\mathcal{E} mapping the orthogonal complement of span⁡{ua}\operatorname{span}\{u_{a}\} isometrically onto that of span⁡{ua′}\operatorname{span}\{u^{\prime}_{a}\}, since both complements have the same dimension. Consequently, the Gram matrix SS determines the point sequence up to a global linear isometry, meaning our scalar statistics (which depend only on SS) are invariant to orthogonal transformations of the embedding space and to strictly positive scaling of the raw unnormalized vectors zj↦cj​zjz_{j}\mapsto c_{j}z_{j}. Furthermore, this formulation allows for an O⁡(d)O(d) streaming state update. When the new state uJu_{J} arrives, computing the latest reversal metric κJ−2\kappa_{J-2} requires SJ−2,J−1S_{J-2,J-1} (computed and stored at the previous step), SJ−1,JS_{J-1,J}, and SJ−2,JS_{J-2,J}. The path length is updated as ℓJ=ℓJ−1+2−2​SJ−1,J\ell_{J}=\ell_{J-1}+\sqrt{2-2S_{J-1,J}}, and the net displacement is updated as δJ=2−2​S1,J\delta_{J}=\sqrt{2-2S_{1,J}}. All three quantities require only evaluating three new inner products in ℝd\mathbb{R}^{d}. Thus, the controller’s state memory can be bounded to just the previous two normalized embeddings uJ−2,uJ−1u_{J-2},u_{J-1}, the initial embedding u1u_{1}, and the running scalar accumulators KJ−1K_{J-1}, ℓJ−1\ell_{J-1}, and SJ−2,J−1S_{J-2,J-1}.

We can unpack the properties of the trajectory by examining the increments. Let Γ\Gamma be the Gram matrix of the increments themselves, with entries Γi​j=⟨ξi,ξj⟩\Gamma_{ij}=\langle\xi_{i},\xi_{j}\rangle for 1≤i,j≤J−11\leq i,j\leq J-1. By expanding the bilinear inner product of ξi=ui+1−ui\xi_{i}=u_{i+1}-u_{i} and ξj=uj+1−uj\xi_{j}=u_{j+1}-u_{j}, we see that Γi​j\Gamma_{ij} is a mixed second difference of the base Gram matrix SS: Γi​j=Si+1,j+1−Si+1,j−Si,j+1+Si,j\Gamma_{ij}=S_{i+1,j+1}-S_{i+1,j}-S_{i,j+1}+S_{i,j}. The diagonal entries are simply the squared step lengths Γj​j=Dj,j+12\Gamma_{jj}=D_{j,j+1}^{2}. The adjacent off-diagonal entries define the reversal signal κj=Γj,j+1=⟨ξj,ξj+1⟩\kappa_{j}=\Gamma_{j,j+1}=\langle\xi_{j},\xi_{j+1}\rangle. By the polarization identity 2​⟨a,b⟩=‖a+b‖2−‖a‖2−‖b‖22\langle a,b\rangle=\|a+b\|^{2}-\|a\|^{2}-\|b\|^{2} applied to a=ξja=\xi_{j} and b=ξj+1b=\xi_{j+1}, noting that a+b=uj+2−uja+b=u_{j+2}-u_{j}, we obtain κj=12​(Dj,j+22−Dj,j+12−Dj+1,j+22)\kappa_{j}=\tfrac{1}{2}(D_{j,j+2}^{2}-D_{j,j+1}^{2}-D_{j+1,j+2}^{2}). Substituting Da,b2=2−2​Sa,bD_{a,b}^{2}=2-2S_{a,b} into this polarization form algebraically recovers the expression in Eq. (2). A reversal occurs when κj<0\kappa_{j}<0, and KJK_{J} counts the number of such reversals. The reversal count can also be read as KJ=(J−2)−#⁡{persistent turns}K_{J}=(J-2)-\#\{\text{persistent turns}\}, where persistent turns are those with κj≥0\kappa_{j}\geq 0. The overall squared net displacement is the sum of all elements in Γ\Gamma, since uJ−u1=∑j=1J−1ξju_{J}-u_{1}=\sum_{j=1}^{J-1}\xi_{j}, meaning δJ2=𝟏⊤​Γ​𝟏\delta_{J}^{2}=\mathbf{1}^{\top}\Gamma\mathbf{1}. Grouping these terms by their lag |i−j||i-j| produces a clear displacement decomposition:

δJ2=𝟏⊤​Γ​𝟏=∑j=1J−1‖ξj‖2+2​∑j=1J−2κj+2​∑h=2J−2∑j=1J−1−h⟨ξj,ξj+h⟩.\delta_{J}^{2}=\mathbf{1}^{\top}\Gamma\mathbf{1}=\sum_{j=1}^{J-1}\|\xi_{j}\|^{2}+2\sum_{j=1}^{J-2}\kappa_{j}+2\sum_{h=2}^{J-2}\sum_{j=1}^{J-1-h}\langle\xi_{j},\xi_{j+h}\rangle. (11)

This exact identity demonstrates the interaction between the net displacement and the local turns: every trajectory reversal (κj<0\kappa_{j}<0) contributes a negative lag-one term that actively reduces the squared net displacement, whereas persistent turns (κj≥0\kappa_{j}\geq 0) add positively to it.

To bound the net-displacement ratio QJ=δJ/ℓJQ_{J}=\delta_{J}/\ell_{J} of Section 3.3, consider paths with ℓJ>0\ell_{J}>0. First, the triangle inequality δJ≤ℓJ\delta_{J}\leq\ell_{J} gives QJ≤1Q_{J}\leq 1. Second, the spatial diameter of the unit sphere limits the displacement to δJ≤‖uJ‖+‖u1‖=2\delta_{J}\leq\|u_{J}\|+\|u_{1}\|=2, yielding QJ≤2/ℓJQ_{J}\leq 2/\ell_{J}. Together, these provide the bound QJ≤min⁡{1,2/ℓJ}Q_{J}\leq\min\{1,2/\ell_{J}\}. As a direct consequence, the condition QJ≤τQQ_{J}\leq\tau_{Q} is implied by the path length alone once ℓJ≥2/τQ\ell_{J}\geq 2/\tau_{Q}, because then QJ≤2/ℓJ≤τQQ_{J}\leq 2/\ell_{J}\leq\tau_{Q}. The converse does not hold: a short path whose endpoint returns close to its start satisfies QJ≤τQQ_{J}\leq\tau_{Q} as well. In this sense τQ\tau_{Q} also acts as a path-length budget for long streams. Furthermore, QJ<1Q_{J}<1 strictly as soon as the sequence visits three distinct points. The Hilbert space ℰ\mathcal{E} is strictly convex. Equality in the triangle inequality δJ=∑j=1J−1‖ξj‖\delta_{J}=\sum_{j=1}^{J-1}\|\xi_{j}\| would force all nonzero step vectors ξj\xi_{j} to be positive scalar multiples of one another. This condition would compel every point uju_{j} to lie on a single ray emanating from u1u_{1}. However, a straight ray can intersect the spherical surface in at most two points. Thus, any trajectory with three or more distinct states must strictly satisfy QJ<1Q_{J}<1.

We can relate the total turning of the trajectory to both the reversal count and the net displacement. Let the step directions be ej=ξj/‖ξj‖∈𝕊d−1e_{j}=\xi_{j}/\|\xi_{j}\|\in\mathbb{S}^{d-1}, and let ΘJ=∑j=1J−2∠⁡(ξj,ξj+1)\Theta_{J}=\sum_{j=1}^{J-2}\angle(\xi_{j},\xi_{j+1}) be the total turning angle. Since a reversal is defined as a turn where κj<0\kappa_{j}<0, equivalent to ∠⁡(ξj,ξj+1)>π/2\angle(\xi_{j},\xi_{j+1})>\pi/2, and all other turns have non-negative angles bounded by π\pi, we immediately have ΘJ≥(π/2)​KJ\Theta_{J}\geq(\pi/2)K_{J}. For the second bound involving QJQ_{J}, connect the consecutive unit direction vectors e1,e2,…,eJ−1e_{1},e_{2},\ldots,e_{J-1} by minimizing great-circle arcs on 𝕊d−1\mathbb{S}^{d-1}. This forms a spherical path known as the tangent indicatrix of the chordal polygon, and its exact arc length is ΘJ\Theta_{J}. If ΘJ≤π\Theta_{J}\leq\pi, let cc be the midpoint of this path by arc length. Every individual direction vector eje_{j} must be within an arc length of ΘJ/2≤π/2\Theta_{J}/2\leq\pi/2 from cc along the path. Because the geodesic distance is bounded by the path distance, the spherical distance from any eje_{j} to cc is at most ΘJ/2\Theta_{J}/2. Taking the cosine of this distance bounds the inner product: ⟨ej,c⟩≥cos⁡(ΘJ/2)\langle e_{j},c\rangle\geq\cos(\Theta_{J}/2). We then project the net displacement onto cc:

δJ=‖∑j=1J−1ξj‖≥⟨∑j=1J−1ξj,c⟩=∑j=1J−1‖ξj‖​⟨ej,c⟩≥cos⁡(ΘJ/2)​∑j=1J−1‖ξj‖=cos⁡(ΘJ/2)​ℓJ.\delta_{J}=\Bigl\|\sum_{j=1}^{J-1}\xi_{j}\Bigr\|\geq\Bigl\langle\sum_{j=1}^{J-1}\xi_{j},c\Bigr\rangle=\sum_{j=1}^{J-1}\|\xi_{j}\|\langle e_{j},c\rangle\geq\cos(\Theta_{J}/2)\sum_{j=1}^{J-1}\|\xi_{j}\|=\cos(\Theta_{J}/2)\,\ell_{J}. (12)

Dividing by ℓJ\ell_{J} shows that QJ≥cos⁡(ΘJ/2)Q_{J}\geq\cos(\Theta_{J}/2). Consequently, a small ratio QJ≤τQQ_{J}\leq\tau_{Q} forces the total turning to be large, ΘJ≥2​arccos⁡τQ\Theta_{J}\geq 2\arccos\tau_{Q}: if ΘJ≤π\Theta_{J}\leq\pi, then cos⁡(ΘJ/2)≤QJ≤τQ\cos(\Theta_{J}/2)\leq Q_{J}\leq\tau_{Q} and the bound follows because the cosine is decreasing on [0,π/2][0,\pi/2]; if ΘJ>π\Theta_{J}>\pi, the bound holds trivially since 2​arccos⁡τQ≤π2\arccos\tau_{Q}\leq\pi for τQ≥0\tau_{Q}\geq 0. This is a discrete form of the classical geometric comparison between chord length and arc length for curves of bounded total curvature (Fenchel, 1929; Milnor, 1950).

Although related, the trajectory reversal count KJK_{J} and the net-displacement ratio QJQ_{J} do not mathematically determine each other. We prove this using two explicit constructions on the sub-sphere 𝕊2⊂𝕊d−1\mathbb{S}^{2}\subset\mathbb{S}^{d-1} parameterized by σ⁡(θ,ϕ)=(cos⁡ϕ​cos⁡θ,cos⁡ϕ​sin⁡θ,sin⁡ϕ)\sigma(\theta,\phi)=(\cos\phi\cos\theta,\cos\phi\sin\theta,\sin\phi). The first construction is a zig-zag with drift: let uj=σ⁡((j−1)​α,(−1)j​β)u_{j}=\sigma\bigl((j-1)\alpha,(-1)^{j}\beta\bigr) with step parameters α=1/(J−1)\alpha=1/(J-1) and β=0.6​α\beta=0.6\alpha. In this trajectory, each step advances by a steady α\alpha in longitude, but alternates in latitude with a total swing of 2​β=1.2​α>α2\beta=1.2\alpha>\alpha. For small steps the chord ξj\xi_{j} is approximately (α,±2​β)(\alpha,\pm 2\beta) in local longitude–latitude coordinates, so that ⟨ξj,ξj+1⟩≈α2−4​β2=−0.44​α2<0\langle\xi_{j},\xi_{j+1}\rangle\approx\alpha^{2}-4\beta^{2}=-0.44\,\alpha^{2}<0: the latitude oscillation dominates, consecutive chords form an obtuse angle, and every turn is a reversal, KJ=J−2K_{J}=J-2. However, because the longitudinal drift is perfectly steady, the net displacement remains a fixed, large fraction of the path length. Specifically, setting J=10J=10 gives K10=8=KoscK_{10}=8=K_{\mathrm{osc}} and Q10=0.619>τQQ_{10}=0.619>\tau_{Q}. The reversal count condition is fully met, but no stop is issued. A direct computation verifies that for this construction, KJ=J−2K_{J}=J-2 and QJ≥0.605Q_{J}\geq 0.605 for all sequence lengths 3≤J≤20003\leq J\leq 2000. The second construction is a loop without reversals: let uj=σ⁡(2​π​(j−1)/(J−1),0)u_{j}=\sigma\bigl(2\pi(j-1)/(J-1),0\bigr) with J−1≥5J-1\geq 5. This traverses the equator exactly once in equal angular steps of ω=2​π/(J−1)<π/2\omega=2\pi/(J-1)<\pi/2. The cosine of the step angle dictates κj=2​cos⁡ω−cos⁡2​ω−1=2​cos⁡ω⁡(1−cos⁡ω)>0\kappa_{j}=2\cos\omega-\cos 2\omega-1=2\cos\omega(1-\cos\omega)>0, which means there are strictly zero reversals and KJ=0K_{J}=0. However, because the path completes a perfect closed circle, the final position matches the first (uJ=u1u_{J}=u_{1}), yielding a net displacement of exactly zero, so QJ=0Q_{J}=0. Here the ratio condition is satisfied, but no stop is issued because there are no reversals.

We can gain intuition for these statistics through several canonical reference models. These are strictly interpretive and do not constitute assumptions made by the controller. For the first model, consider equicorrelated streams where Sa,b=ρ<1S_{a,b}=\rho<1 for all distinct a≠ba\neq b. By substitution, κj=ρ−1<0\kappa_{j}=\rho-1<0 everywhere, so reversals happen at every step and KJ=J−2K_{J}=J-2. The path length evaluates to ℓJ=(J−1)​2−2​ρ\ell_{J}=(J-1)\sqrt{2-2\rho} and the displacement is identically δJ=2−2​ρ\delta_{J}=\sqrt{2-2\rho}, which yields QJ=1/(J−1)Q_{J}=1/(J-1), remarkably independent of the correlation parameter ρ\rho. If we deploy the reference limits (Kosc,τQ)=(8,0.14)(K_{\mathrm{osc}},\tau_{Q})=(8,0.14), such an equicorrelated stream first satisfies the trajectory-stop condition exactly at J=10J=10, because K10=8K_{10}=8 and Q10=1/9<0.14Q_{10}=1/9<0.14. In this view, a stream with no coherent temporal structure is stopped at its very first admissible segment, and each persistent turn encountered postpones the stop. For a second model, consider stationary streams where Sa,b=ρ⁡(|a−b|)S_{a,b}=\rho(|a-b|) for some positive-definite correlation function ρ\rho with ρ⁡(0)=1\rho(0)=1. The reversal metric evaluates to κj=2​ρ​(1)−ρ⁡(2)−1=γ⁡(2)−2​γ​(1)\kappa_{j}=2\rho(1)-\rho(2)-1=\gamma(2)-2\gamma(1), where γ⁡(h)=1−ρ⁡(h)=12​Da,a+h2\gamma(h)=1-\rho(h)=\tfrac{1}{2}D_{a,a+h}^{2} is the variogram of the process. A reversal thus corresponds to local sub-additivity of the variogram, γ⁡(2)<2​γ​(1)\gamma(2)<2\gamma(1). The critical boundary γ⁡(2)=2​γ​(1)\gamma(2)=2\gamma(1) is attained by sequences with orthogonal consecutive increments, which serves as the discrete counterpart to Kolmogorov’s Wiener spiral in Hilbert space (Kolmogorov, 1940). Within stationary processes, mean-reverting streams such as the autoregressive ρ⁡(h)=e−λ​h\rho(h)=e^{-\lambda h} will reverse at every single turn because κj=−(1−e−λ)2<0\kappa_{j}=-(1-e^{-\lambda})^{2}<0. In stark contrast, a steady rotating stream described by ρ⁡(h)=cos⁡(ω​h)\rho(h)=\cos(\omega h) with angular step 0<ω<π/20<\omega<\pi/2 never reverses at all. On this interpretive reading, KJK_{J} measures the accumulated elapsed history restricted only to non-persistent turns. Persistent turns—where the stream maintains its prior direction—act as the events that continually hold the trajectory stop back.

The net-displacement ratio QJQ_{J} possesses a direct maximum-likelihood interpretation in directional statistics. Suppose we model the normalized directions of motion ej=ξj/‖ξj‖e_{j}=\xi_{j}/\|\xi_{j}\| as draws from a von Mises–Fisher distribution on 𝕊d−1\mathbb{S}^{d-1}. The density is f⁡(e)∝exp⁡(β⁡⟨μ,e⟩)f(e)\propto\exp(\beta\langle\mu,e\rangle), where μ\mu is the mean direction and β\beta is the concentration parameter. We weight each observation by its spatial step size ‖ξj‖\|\xi_{j}\|, yielding an arc-length-weighted log-likelihood proportional to ∑j=1J−1‖ξj‖​log⁡f⁡(ej)\sum_{j=1}^{J-1}\|\xi_{j}\|\log f(e_{j}). Expanding this sum gives ℓJ​log⁡Cd​(β)+β⁡⟨μ,∑j=1J−1ξj⟩\ell_{J}\log C_{d}(\beta)+\beta\langle\mu,\sum_{j=1}^{J-1}\xi_{j}\rangle, which equals ℓJ​log⁡Cd​(β)+β⁡⟨μ,uJ−u1⟩\ell_{J}\log C_{d}(\beta)+\beta\langle\mu,u_{J}-u_{1}\rangle, where Cd​(β)C_{d}(\beta) is the required normalizing constant. For any β>0\beta>0 this is maximized over unit vectors μ\mu by aligning μ\mu with the net displacement, μ^=(uJ−u1)/δJ\hat{\mu}=(u_{J}-u_{1})/\delta_{J}, which leaves ℓJ​log⁡Cd​(β)+β​δJ\ell_{J}\log C_{d}(\beta)+\beta\delta_{J}. Since Cd​(β)=βd/2−1/((2​π)d/2​Id/2−1​(β))C_{d}(\beta)=\beta^{d/2-1}/\bigl((2\pi)^{d/2}I_{d/2-1}(\beta)\bigr) and Iν′​(β)=Iν+1​(β)+(ν/β)​Iν​(β)I_{\nu}^{\prime}(\beta)=I_{\nu+1}(\beta)+(\nu/\beta)I_{\nu}(\beta), one has dd​βlogCd(β)=−Id/2(β)/Id/2−1(β)\frac{d}{d\beta}\log C_{d}(\beta)=-I_{d/2}(\beta)/I_{d/2-1}(\beta). Setting the derivative −ℓJId/2(β)/Id/2−1(β)+δJ-\ell_{J}\,I_{d/2}(\beta)/I_{d/2-1}(\beta)+\delta_{J} to zero shows that the fitted concentration β^\hat{\beta} is characterized by the ratio of modified Bessel functions Ad​(β^)=Id/2​(β^)/Id/2−1​(β^)A_{d}(\hat{\beta})=I_{d/2}(\hat{\beta})/I_{d/2-1}(\hat{\beta}) must exactly equal QJQ_{J} (Mardia and Jupp, 2000; Banerjee et al., 2005). Since AdA_{d} increases strictly monotonically from 00 to 11, observing QJQ_{J} is mathematically equivalent to observing the fitted concentration of the directions of motion. Thresholding QJQ_{J} is therefore thresholding this concentration. For an embedding space of dimension d=4096d=4096, the reference threshold τQ=0.14\tau_{Q}=0.14 corresponds to a fitted concentration of β^≈585\hat{\beta}\approx 585.

Finally, we analyze the stability of these geometric quantities under small embedding perturbations, such as those caused by reduced-precision arithmetic or numerical batching in the embedding service. Let zj,zj′∈ℝd∖{0}z_{j},z^{\prime}_{j}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}\setminus\{0\} be two sets of raw unnormalized embeddings, which normalize to uju_{j} and uj′u^{\prime}_{j} respectively. Let η=maxj⁡‖uj−uj′‖\eta=\max_{j}\|u_{j}-u^{\prime}_{j}\| be the maximum normalized perturbation. To bound η\eta in terms of the raw vectors, let a=‖zj‖a=\|z_{j}\|, b=‖zj′‖b=\|z^{\prime}_{j}\|, and c=⟨zj,zj′⟩/(a​b)c=\langle z_{j},z^{\prime}_{j}\rangle/(ab). Expanding the norms yields ‖uj−uj′‖2=2−2​c\|u_{j}-u^{\prime}_{j}\|^{2}=2-2c and ‖zj−zj′‖2=a2+b2−2​a​b​c\|z_{j}-z^{\prime}_{j}\|^{2}=a^{2}+b^{2}-2abc.
