Appendix C Experimental details

C.1 Benchmarks, metrics, and task contracts

CSQA.

We use the 1,221 validation questions of CommonsenseQA (Talmor et al., 2019), each with five options. GLOBE answers zero-shot with the option letter in a box, decoded at temperature 0, and a fixed answer parser maps the visible answer to one of the five labels; the metric is accuracy.

GSM8K.

We use the 1,319 test problems of GSM8K (Cobbe et al., 2021) with a fixed five-shot exemplar manifest, and score strict exact match of the final #### answer.

BFCL v4 Live.

Because the live split of BFCL v4 (Patil et al., 2025) is revised upstream, we evaluate a frozen 2,251-item snapshot rather than following the live revision. The snapshot contains 1,335 AST items—258 simple, 1,037 multiple, 16 parallel, and 24 parallel-multiple calls—and 916 relevance- and irrelevance-detection items, namely 16 relevance questions and 900 irrelevance questions, 25 of which this snapshot stores in the relevance file. The upstream live files as of 2026-09-26 regroup the same 2,251 items as 1,351 AST and 900 detection items, so absolute scores are comparable only within one snapshot. Tool schemas are rendered by the model’s chat template, calls are parsed by the serving stack’s native tool-call parser, and the score is the item-weighted accuracy over all live items under the official AST and detection checkers.

BFCL v4 Agent Memory.

Each of the three memory backends (KV, Vector, Recursive Sum) has 192 tasks, of which 37 are prerequisite conversations that populate the memory and 155 are scored. Every model step is one controlled request with a 16,384-token retained budget. Table 1 reports the equal-weight mean of the three official backend accuracies, the sum of the three backends’ active wall times, and the official per-task output tokens averaged over the backends.

Character-LLM.

We use the 857 single-turn interview questions of Character-LLM (Shao et al., 2023), whose original evaluation rubric scores five aspects on a 1–7 Likert scale. We use a four-aspect adaptation of that rubric: an independent judge model scores memorization, personality, values, and hallucination and omits stability. We report the normalized acting score NAS=100​(s¯−1)/6\mathrm{NAS}=100\,(\bar{s}-1)/6 for the mean aspect score s¯\bar{s}; NAS is our normalization of the mean judge score, not the metric defined in the original paper. The judge is cyankiwi/Qwen3.8-27B-AWQ-INT4 (4-bit AWQ weights, group size 32, ModelScope revision ffb29de) served with vLLM in non-thinking mode at temperature 0. All methods are judged by the same judge on the same 857 questions.

Answer parsing and evaluation.

Gemma and Qwen follow the same task-specific answer-parsing and evaluation protocol described above.

C.2 Baselines

All baselines use the same models, benchmark items, and vLLM serving stack as GLOBE and follow their method-native contracts. Nothink disables the thinking channel through the chat template and answers directly. Full CoT leaves thinking unconstrained up to the task’s budget. DEER (Yang et al., 2026) issues a short boxed trial answer at reflection markers such as Wait and exits once the trial’s confidence passes its threshold; it has neither a trajectory stop nor a phase switch. ThinkBrake (Song et al., 2026) compares, at every sentence boundary, the log-probability of the most likely continuation token with that of the thinking-close token, and closes thinking once the margin falls below a task-level threshold τ\tau. RCPD (Wei et al., 2026) tracks the rank of the thinking-close token at sentence boundaries and force-closes thinking with its published reasoning-dynamics rules. ThinkBrake and RCPD issue no trial requests.

C.3 Cost accounting

Output tokens.

For GSM8K, CSQA, BFCL v4 Live, and Character-LLM the token column counts the retained output of the main stream—reasoning plus visible answer—re-encoded with the model’s own tokenizer from the stored strings, with the appended close marker included for early-exited items. Trial requests, discarded trial text, and prompts are excluded; the first two are reported separately in Appendix D.2. Main-stream tokens decoded after the frozen prefix of an accepted trial are discarded with the stream and excluded as well; their elapsed time is covered by active E2E. Agent Memory uses the official per-task output token counts.

Active E2E time.

E2E is the wall time during which the run’s requests are active, including the main stream, trial requests, embedding requests, and continuations. For Agent Memory it is the sum over the three backends, and for Character-LLM, which runs one item at a time, the sum of per-item latencies. Overlapping generation and embedding work is counted once in wall time.

Aggregate reductions.

The reductions quoted in Section 4 compare each GLOBE cell with the Full CoT cell of the same model and task and average the ten per-pair reductions with equal weight, rather than pooling token or time volumes; Appendix D.1 lists the ten pairs and the mean excluding Qwen BFCL v4 Live.

C.4 Serving and compute

All generation runs on NVIDIA A100 80GB PCIe GPUs with vLLM 0.22.1. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B is served with tensor parallelism 4, a 200K context window, prefix caching, and raw log-probabilities for the top-5 candidates; Gemma-4-12B-it is served with tensor parallelism 2. The segment encoder Qwen3-Embedding-8B runs as a separate vLLM embedding service on one GPU. Trials and continuations go to the same generation endpoint as the main stream so that its prefix cache is reused.

Appendix D Additional results

This appendix extends the three experimental questions of Section 4. Appendices D.1 and D.2 break the cost savings down by model–task pair and by request type; Appendices D.3 and D.4 extend the stop-reliability analysis to CSQA and to Gemma; Appendices D.6 and D.7 extend the component ablation to CSQA and Character-LLM; Appendices D.8 and D.9 report the net-displacement-ratio threshold sweep and the sensitivity to the segment encoder; and Appendix D.10 compares the candidate signals of the trial phase.

D.1 Per-pair accuracy and cost changes

Table 4 shows that the savings of Section 4.2 are not carried by a few favorable pairs. GLOBE shortens all ten pairs, with token reductions from 7.7%7.7\% to 78.6%78.6\% and E2E reductions from 27.7%27.7\% to 76.0%76.0\%; the E2E speed-up is at least 1.38×1.38\times everywhere and reaches 4.17×4.17\times on Qwen CSQA. Accuracy moves by at most 3.53.5 points: six of the ten pairs gain, led by Gemma BFCL v4 Live at +3.5+3.5 and Qwen Agent Memory at +3.0+3.0 points, and no pair loses more than 2.12.1 points. The largest token savings fall on the tasks where Full CoT writes the longest traces, namely Agent Memory and CSQA on Qwen, where the trajectory stop has the most repetition to remove.

D.2 Controller overhead

Controller overhead in wall time.

Trials are rare and short: at most 1.361.36 per item, with at most 2020 discarded trial tokens per item, which is 0.04%0.04\%, 0.5%0.5\%, and 5.4%5.4\% of the retained output on CSQA, GSM8K, and BFCL v4 Live. An item issues two to three requests in total, and each trial or continuation re-uses the prefix cache of the main stream, as detailed in Appendix A.6. Embedding requests take at most 13.6%13.6\% of the per-item wall time and overlap with generation, so the E2E reductions of Table 4 already include the time overhead of trials, continuations, and the geometric observer.

The phase switch prunes trials.

The one-way phase switch also bounds the trial budget. Relative to the full-GLOBE run of the same sweep, allowing trials in the trajectory phase on BFCL v4 Live with Qwen raises the number of trials launched over the split by 54%54\%, from 3,1083{,}108 to 4,7814{,}781, and the active E2E time by 4.5%4.5\%, from 3,1973{,}197 to 3,3423{,}342 seconds, while accuracy changes by less than 0.5%0.5\%. Retiring these trials therefore saves requests.

D.3 Stop coverage versus stop quality

Coverage alone cannot rank early-exit controllers, because stopping every trace would be reported as full coverage. Table 6 therefore pairs each controller’s stop rate with the accuracy among exactly those stopped items, and with their product, the share of all items that are stopped early and answered correctly, which is the green segment of Figure 3b. The stop rate is the share of items that the controller itself stops, so a natural close never counts as a stop. Besides the three tasks of Figure 3b, the table adds CSQA.

GLOBE has the highest yield on all four tasks.

GLOBE converts the largest share of items into correct early exits on every task: 85.0%85.0\% on CSQA, 95.2%95.2\% on GSM8K, 53.3%53.3\% on BFCL v4 Live, and 27.7%27.7\% on Agent Memory, ahead of the best baseline by 3.13.1, 5.75.7, 6.86.8, and 8.18.1 points. On CSQA and GSM8K it combines the highest coverage at 98.6%98.6\% and 98.9%98.9\% with diagnostic post-stop accuracies of 86.2%86.2\% and 96.3%96.3\%.

The baselines fail on different axes.

ThinkBrake is the most accurate on the items it stops on CSQA at 87.6%87.6\% but reaches only 69.9%69.9\% coverage there, never triggers on GSM8K, and stops 5.8%5.8\% of BFCL v4 Live. DEER needs a reflection marker followed by a confident trial, so its coverage stays between 36.8%36.8\% and 65.4%65.4\% and its post-stop accuracy on CSQA is 77.7%77.7\%, 8.5%8.5\% below GLOBE’s. RCPD covers the most items after GLOBE on CSQA and GSM8K, but on BFCL v4 Live the 77.7%77.7\% of items it closes are only 59.8%59.8\% correct, against 76.0%76.0\% for GLOBE: coverage bought by closing the stream before the call structure settles is paid for in accuracy. On Agent Memory RCPD’s stopped items are slightly more accurate at 64.1%64.1\% against 59.2%59.2\%, but it stops only 30.5%30.5\% of the items, so its yield is 19.6%19.6\% against 27.7%27.7\%. Read as a pair, no baseline reaches GLOBE’s coverage at GLOBE’s post-stop accuracy on any task.

D.4 Stop reliability on both models

Table 7 repeats the harm–rescue analysis of Figure 3a on Gemma. The pattern transfers across model families. On GSM8K, Gemma’s early stops rescue 40.0%40.0\% of the items that Full CoT gets wrong while harming 3.14%3.14\% of those it gets right; on BFCL v4 Live its two rates, 4.14%4.14\% and 9.75%9.75\%, are within 0.2%0.2\% of Qwen’s. On both models, successful early answers are observed even on items that Full CoT answers incorrectly.

D.5 Gemma GSM8K without the trajectory stop

Table 2 reports 62.2%62.2\% for Gemma on GSM8K without the trajectory stop. This run keeps the phase switch and the trial branch, and its items fall into three mutually exclusive outcomes:

Outcome Items Correct
Trial stop 111 92
Natural close without budget exhaustion 737 728
No trial stop, budget exhausted 471 0
Total 1,319 820

All 471471 items that reach the 8,1928{,}192-token budget without a trial stop are answered incorrectly, whereas 728728 of the 737737 natural closes are correct. The loss therefore comes from traces that keep reasoning until the budget runs out, which is the behavior the trajectory stop is designed to cut.

D.6 CSQA remove-one ablation

The trajectory stop is the load-bearing component on CSQA as well. Removing it costs 127127 correct items on Qwen and 107107 on Gemma, that is, 10.410.4 and 8.88.8 points, with p=2×10−24p=2\times 10^{-24} and 5×10−115\times 10^{-11}. It also collapses the early-stop share from 97.0%97.0\% and 76.7%76.7\% to 1.9%1.9\% and 8.0%8.0\% and multiplies the retained reasoning by 6.86.8 and 7.77.7, consistent with a model that keeps re-examining options it has already ruled out and eventually talks itself out of the right one. The other three removals stay within noise on this task with |Δ|≤16|\Delta|\leq 16 items and p≥0.12p\geq 0.12, and move the token count by at most 15%15\%, so the trial phase and the τQ\tau_{Q} gate act as safeguards rather than as the main exit.

D.7 Character-LLM remove-one ablation

On role-play the trajectory stop acts as a cost control rather than an accuracy control. Disabling it raises NAS by at most 1.81.8 points while the retained reasoning grows 2.78×2.78\times on Qwen and 1.43×1.43\times on Gemma, and on Gemma 1414 of the 857857 interviews then fail to return an answer inside the 2,0482{,}048-token budget, so the stop is also what keeps role-play generation bounded. The τQ\tau_{Q} gate is the component that protects answer quality here: removing it lowers NAS by 2.052.05 points on Gemma with p=8.5×10−4p=8.5\times 10^{-4}, consistent with the veto holding back stops while the character’s answer is still being developed. Because the role-play harness has no trial phase, the phase switch here only acts as the warm-up gate that keeps the trajectory stop from arming before nminn_{\min} completed segments. The first accepted stops already fall after this gate, so removing the switch is a negative control: NAS changes by at most 0.16%0.16\% with p≥0.80p\geq 0.80, and the token count stays at 1.00×1.00\times and 1.01×1.01\times. No removal yields a significant NAS gain without raising the cost.

D.8 Operating-point sweeps on BFCL v4 Live

Table 10 reports the net-displacement-ratio threshold sweep on all N=2,251N=2{,}251 BFCL v4 Live items with Qwen.

Loosening the gate from 0.060.06 to 0.140.14 raises the number of trajectory stops by 368368, from 699699 to 1,0671{,}067, and cuts the retained reasoning by 25%25\% and the E2E time by 8%8\%. At 0.140.14, we observe the highest accuracy in this threshold sweep. Beyond 0.140.14 the stop count saturates at 1,0301{,}030–1,0811{,}081 and the token count at 237237–254254, yielding at most modest extra token savings alongside 1515–3030 fewer correct items. We select 0.140.14 as the knee at which the saving saturates.

The default setting (Kphase,Kosc,τQ)=(4,8,0.14)(K_{\mathrm{phase}},K_{\mathrm{osc}},\tau_{Q})=(4,8,0.14), already reported in Section 4.5, yields 1,8001{,}800 correct answers out of 2,2512{,}251, an accuracy of 79.96%, together with 240.9 retained reasoning tokens per item and 1,0671{,}067 trajectory stops.

D.9 Sensitivity to the segment encoder

GLOBE embeds every completed segment with Qwen3-Embedding-8B. To test whether the trajectory stop depends on this particular encoder, we run GLOBE on Qwen with the reference configuration, which uses sent80 segmentation, (Kphase,Kosc,τQ)=(4,8,0.14)(K_{\mathrm{phase}},K_{\mathrm{osc}},\tau_{Q})=(4,8,0.14), and the trial settings of Appendix A.5. We replace only the encoder, by Qwen3-Embedding-4B or Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B, each served as its own vLLM embedding instance, on BFCL v4 Live and on GSM8K.

Accuracy and stop counts are similar with a 13-fold smaller encoder.

On BFCL v4 Live the trajectory stop closes 1,0631{,}063 items with either smaller encoder against 1,0671{,}067 with the default one, and on GSM8K 1,0301{,}030 and 1,0351{,}035 items against 1,0321{,}032. The retained reasoning stays within 2%2\% of the default encoder on both tasks, at 236236–243243 tokens on BFCL v4 Live and 357357–363363 on GSM8K. Accuracy changes by at most 0.84%0.84\%, and no change is significant, with all p>0.05p>0.05; on GSM8K the 4B encoder answers six more items than the default encoder and the 0.6B encoder the same number. Active E2E time does not vary systematically with encoder size. The robustness can be plausibly explained by the construction of Section 3.3: the stopping statistics depend only on the angles between segment embeddings, and the reversal test only on the sign of κj\kappa_{j}, so the decisions can be insensitive to encoder changes if they preserve the coarse geometry of the trace. A smaller encoder also shortens the embedding time per item by up to 39%39\%, from 0.950.95 to 0.580.58 seconds on GSM8K, which lowers the footprint of the geometric observer measured in Appendix D.2.

D.10 Which candidate signal authorizes an early exit

For Figure 1a, trial events are binned by the completed-segment index J−2J-2, with each bin placed at its median reasoning-token count.

The marker lane of Figure 1 pools three candidate signals, and they are not interchangeable. Pooled over the deployment-conditioned population the thinking-close signal reaches a gate rate of 21.1%21.1\% and a yield of 16.8%16.8\%, Wait reaches 14.7%14.7\% and 8.9%8.9\%, and Actually reaches 7.9%7.9\% and 4.5%4.5\%. Figure 5 shows why pooling them hides the structure: the close signal’s gate rate and yield climb to 40%40\% and 35%35\% at 400400 tokens, whereas Wait peaks at 27%27\% and 17%17\% around 100100 tokens and then decays, and Actually stays below 13%13\% and 9%9\% at every position. A reflection marker is therefore associated with a weaker trial yield, while the thinking-close signal demonstrates a higher observed yield. This changing signal mixture partly explains why the pooled marker lane of Figure 1 decays: after 400400 tokens its events are increasingly textual markers rather than close signals. The bottom panel of Figure 5 shows the second half of the window argument. Up to 700700 tokens the marker lane loses yield because its confidence test passes less often, from 29%29\% at 100100–200200 tokens down to 13%13\% at 600600–700700, not because the answers get worse. Beyond 800800 tokens both fail at once: the confidence test keeps passing and the mean trial confidence stays flat near 0.800.80, but the share of passed tests whose answer is correct collapses from 78%78\% to 45%45\%. This lower late pooled accepted-answer quality despite stable mean confidence motivates retiring trials.

Appendix E Case studies

This appendix walks through five items. The four Qwen items come from the GLOBE runs behind Table 1, and the Gemma item from a GLOBE run on the same split. Reasoning excerpts are verbatim and trimmed with […]; the red marker shows where GLOBE ends the main stream and what it observes there. JJ is the number of completed segments, KK the reversal count, and QQ the net-displacement ratio at the stop.

E.1 Trial-answer exit at a thinking-close signal

BFCL v4 Live, Qwen (live_multiple_829-178-4). User: “Can you play ‘Bohemian Rhapsody’ in the kitchen for me?”
GLOBE reasoning (109 retained tokens): The user wants to play the song ‘Bohemian Rhapsody’ in the kitchen. I need to use the Music_3_PlayMedia function. Parameters required: track: “Bohemian Rhapsody”; device: “Kitchen”; artist: optional, default “any”; album: optional, default “any”. I will call Music_3_PlayMedia with track="Bohemian Rhapsody" and device="Kitchen". All [GLOBE stops: </think> enters the top-5 at J=3J=3; trial {Music_3_PlayMedia(track="Bohemian Rhapsody", device="Kitchen")}, q=0.945>τconfq=0.945>\tau_{\mathrm{conf}}]
GLOBE answer: Music_3_PlayMedia(track="Bohemian Rhapsody", device="Kitchen") (correct)
Full CoT: writes the same call in its first paragraph, then keeps confirming it: “[Final Output Generation] →\rightarrow {"name": "Music_3_PlayMedia", …} Done. Proceeds. (Self-Correction/Verification during thought) Wait, I should check if there are any other constraints. None. Proceeds. […]” The loop runs until the token budget is exhausted, and no call is emitted (wrong)

The model’s own thinking-close token enters the top-5 candidates after three segments, when the call and both arguments are already fixed; the trial branch confirms it with confidence 0.9450.945 and the continuation emits exactly that call after 109 reasoning tokens. Full CoT has the same call in hand at the same point but never commits to it: it restates it until the budget runs out.

E.2 Trajectory stop on an argument that keeps flipping

BFCL v4 Live, Qwen (live_multiple_455-145-6). User: “Search for free entry gardens suitable for a short trip in London, UK?”
GLOBE reasoning (311 retained tokens; one trial, {London, UK} at q=0.769q=0.769, rejected): […] category: “Park” or “Nature Preserve” might be closest to “gardens”, but the user said “gardens”. […] I’ll use “Park” or “dontcare” and filter by free_entry. Actually, “Park” is the best match for gardens. Or I can just leave category as “dontcare” and rely on free_entry. Let’s stick to “Park” or “dontcare”. I’ll use “dontcare” to be safe, or maybe “Park”. Actually, gardens are often categorized as Parks. I’ll use “Park”. Wait, the prompt says “gardens”. I’ll just use “dontcare” for category to be safe, or “Park”. Let’s use “Park”. […] Let’s check the parameters: [GLOBE stops: J=10J=10, K=8K=8, Q=0.127≤τQQ=0.127\leq\tau_{Q}]
GLOBE answer: Travel_1_FindAttractions(location="London, UK", category="Park", free_entry="True", good_for_kids="dontcare") (correct)
Full CoT: settles on the same arguments early, then alternates between “[Output Generation] →\rightarrow Tool Call.” and “[Final Output Generation] →\rightarrow Tool Call. […] Done. Proceeds.” until the token budget is exhausted, and no call is emitted (wrong)

The trace has already collected every argument; what remains is a choice between two enum values that it revisits sentence after sentence. On the unit sphere these sentences alternate between two nearby directions, so every new segment reverses the previous step while the path makes almost no net progress: after ten segments the reversal count reaches Kosc=8K_{\mathrm{osc}}=8 with a net-displacement ratio of 0.1270.127, and GLOBE ends the stream after 311 reasoning tokens. The continuation commits to "Park" and returns a correct call. Full CoT resolves the same dilemma, but then loops on its own output and never closes; this is the failure that the trajectory stop is designed to cut.

E.3 Phase switch and a trajectory stop that rescues an answer

GSM8K, Qwen (test item 100). Question: “Jerome had 4 friends who came to visit him on a certain day. The first friend pressed on the doorbell 20 times before Jerome opened, the second friend pressed on the doorbell 1/4 times more than Jerome’s first friend. The third friend pressed on the doorbell 10 times more than the fourth friend. If the fourth friend pressed on the doorbell 60 times, how many doorbell rings did the doorbell make?” (gold: 175)
Trial phase: three thinking-close trials at J=2,4,5J=2,4,5 return {10}, {135}, and {135} with confidence 0.5870.587, 0.7090.709, and 0.7550.755; all are rejected. The reversal count then passes Kphase=4K_{\mathrm{phase}}=4 and trials are retired.
GLOBE reasoning (659 retained tokens): […] Sum = 20 + 25 + 70 + 60 = 175. 4. Check for Ambiguities/Traps: […] “10 times more than” usually means original + 10. Wait, “10 times more than” can be ambiguous. It could mean 10 * F4 = 600, or F4 + 10 = 70. […] Actually, “10 times more than” strictly means multiplication by 10 (or 11x depending on interpretation), but in elementary math problems, it’s often a typo for “10 more than”. Let’s check typical patterns in these datasets. Often, “X times more than” means addition if X is small, but here it says “10 times more than”. [GLOBE stops: J=15J=15, K=13K=13, Q=0.096Q=0.096]
GLOBE answer: “The third friend pressed it 10 times more than the fourth friend: 60 + 10 = 70 times. Total doorbell rings = 20 + 25 + 70 + 60 = 175.” (correct)
Full CoT answer: “The third friend pressed 10 times more than the fourth, which is 10 * 60 = 600 times. The total number of doorbell rings is 20 + 25 + 600 + 60 = 705.” (wrong)

This item exercises all three components. The early trials are launched while the computation is unfinished and return wrong answers (1010 and 135135); their confidence stays below τconf\tau_{\mathrm{conf}}, so none of them ends the stream. Once the reversal count reaches KphaseK_{\mathrm{phase}}, trials are retired, and the trajectory records the trace circling between two readings of “10 times more than”. Thirteen reversals with a net-displacement ratio of 0.0960.096 end the stream while the trace is still at its first, correct computation, and the continuation answers 175175. Full CoT keeps deliberating, settles on the other reading, and answers 705705: an instance of the rescue measured in Figure 3a.

E.4 Trajectory stop on a multiple-choice trace

CSQA, Qwen (validation-000124). Question: “From where do aliens arrive?” (A) outer space (B) weekly world news (C) roswell (D) universe (E) mars (gold: A)
GLOBE reasoning (345 retained tokens, no trial): […] (A) outer space: This is the general location where extraterrestrial life is hypothesized to exist. […] (D) universe: While true in a broad sense, “outer space” is the specific medium through which they travel to Earth. […] While they might come from Mars (E) or the Universe (D), “outer space” (A) is the most encompassing and standard answer […] However, let’s look at the structure of the question. It looks like a common sense or trivia question. [GLOBE stops: J=10J=10, K=8K=8, Q=0.135≤τQQ=0.135\leq\tau_{Q}]
GLOBE answer: \boxed{A} (correct)

The trace reweighs options already ruled out, causing the reversal count to grow while net displacement stays small (K=8K=8, Q=0.135Q=0.135 after 10 segments). GLOBE stops after 345 reasoning tokens with the correct option.

E.5 An early trial on Gemma

GSM8K, Gemma (test item 298). Question: “Carmen goes to an auction to win an antique desk. She accepts the opening bid of $200 and continues bidding until she wins. The bids on the desk rise by $50 each time and 3 other people each bid once. Carmen bids after each of the 3 other people and eventually wins. How much money, in dollars, does the desk cost her?” (gold: 500)
GLOBE reasoning (105 retained tokens): […] Opening bid: $200 (Carmen accepts this). Bids rise by $50 each time. There are 3 other people who each bid once. Carmen bids *after* each of the 3 other people. Carmen eventually wins. Goal: Find the final cost of the desk. Initial state: Carmen accepts the opening bid of $200. [GLOBE stops: Wait at J=2J=2; trial {350}, q=0.925>τconfq=0.925>\tau_{\mathrm{conf}}]
GLOBE answer (continuation from the retained prefix): “[…] The second other person bids: $300 + $50 = $350. Carmen bids after the second person: $350 + $50 = $400. The third other person bids: $400 + $50 = $450. Carmen bids after the third person to win: $450 + $50 = $500. The desk costs her $500.” (correct)
Full CoT: exhausts its 8,192-token budget without a final answer (wrong)

The trial answers readiness, not the value of the final answer: its numeral {350} is only a probe and is not inherited by the continuation, which produces the visible answer afterwards from the retained prefix under the task’s own format. Here the prefix has already laid out every rule of the auction, and the continuation carries the computation through to $500 in the visible answer, while Full CoT on the same item never reaches an answer inside its budget.
